ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is a trapezoid, AB is the upper horizontal base, labeled 50; DC is the lower horizontal base, parallel to AB but not directly labeled with a length. The left side AD is an oblique side, labeled 15; the right side BC is an oblique side, labeled 20. In the figure, a perpendicular has been drawn from a point on AB to DC, the height is labeled 12, and there is a right-angle mark. The two oblique sides AD and BC both slant outward relative to the upper base, so the lower base DC is longer than the upper base AB by the two horizontal offsets on the left and right. Then reason: Draw perpendiculars from A and B respectively to the lower base DC. The left oblique side AD=15 and height 12 form a right triangle, and the left horizontal offset is sqrt(15^2-12^2)=sqrt(225-144)=sqrt(81)=9. The right oblique side BC=20 and height 12 form a right triangle, and the right horizontal offset is sqrt(20^2-12^2)=sqrt(400-144)=sqrt(256)=16. Therefore the lower base DC=9+50+16=75. The area of the trapezoid = ((upper base+lower base)/2)×height = ((50+75)/2)×12 = 125/2×12 = 750.
